title: Heuristic-driven prefetch and weight lease protocol
body:
Summary:
This document proposes a heuristic-driven prefetch subsystem and a lightweight weight-lease protocol to improve tail latency, reduce IO storms, and make hot-swap operations safer for large sharded models served by the runtime. The two pieces work together: the prefetcher predicts near-future parameter access and primes local memory/mmap regions, while the lease protocol establishes transient ownership of weight fragments to coordinate eviction, hot-swap, and checkpoint commits without global locking.

Motivation and goals:
- Reduce cold-start token latency spikes caused by many concurrent requests touching distinct shards.
- Avoid large synchronous IO on eviction by providing coordinated leases and soft-expiry so in-flight requests can finish using a fragment while ownership is transferred.
- Make hot-swap (model binary replacement) safer by enabling transfer of leases and graceful background rehydration of parameters.
- Keep runtime complexity bounded: minimal blocking paths, stateless-ish heuristics, and clear telemetries for tuning.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Model parameters are sharded into fragments (shards, pages, tiles) and are addressable by fragment id and model-version tag.
- Underlying storage supports mmap-backed reads and safetensors unpack + mapped backing when possible.
- Nodes run multiple worker threads/engines that may share GPU or CPU memory pools; lease metadata must be compact and cheap to check.
- Networked storage (S3) is high-latency compared to local NVMe; prefetch aims to hide that latency.

High-level design:
1) Prefetch subsystem (heuristic-driven):
   - Input signals:
     * Request routing trace: sequence of token positions and layer indices for recent requests per route/model.
     * KV-cache hit patterns: which layers/sequences commonly reuse cached KV slots.
     * Per-fragment access counters (LRU-ish but time-decayed).
     * Model invocation metadata: sequence length, sampling strategy (deterministic vs streaming), candidate beam count.
   - Heuristics (pluggable):
     * Prefix-based: if route X commonly touches fragments set F within first N tokens, prefetch F when a request arrives with prefix length < N.
     * Layer-priority: prioritize attention and MLP fragments that historically cause stalls at token step T.
     * Probabilistic lookahead: sample top-K next-token predictions to identify likely next-path fragments for conditional compute; used only for long-running sessions.
   - Actions:
     * Async mmap-touch: schedule background mmap page faults for predicted fragments to warm OS page cache and runtime residency.
     * Early deserialize: for safetensors-packed fragments, kick off async unpack to a preallocated staging buffer if prediction confidence > threshold.
     * Batch prefetch: coalesce requests for fragments across concurrent sessions within a short time window (configurable, e.g. 8-20ms).
   - Safety knobs:
     * Max prefetch bandwidth: configurable percent of IO bandwidth to avoid starving foreground IO.
     * In-flight limit: cap number of fragments prefetched per request to bound memory pressure.
     * Fallback suppression: if eviction pressure is high, downgrade to 'touch-only' prefetch rather than full deserialize.

2) Weight lease protocol (lightweight transient ownership):
   - Terminology:
     * Fragment: smallest addressable weight block (tile/page/shard).
     * Lease: a short-lived token indicating a worker has the right to assume the fragment will not be evicted or mutated without coordination.
     * Lease-holder: worker thread/process that currently holds a lease for a fragment.
   - Lease semantics:
     * Duration: short (e.g., default 2s, tunable by model and route).
     * Renewals: lease-holder can renew atomically if still actively using fragment; renew rate limited to prevent thundering renewals.
     * Soft-expiry: on expiry, other processes may request a transfer; original holder may continue to use fragment for a grace window (soft-expiry + 100ms) to drain in-flight ops.
     * Transfer: explicit hand-off where new holder requests transfer and previous holder commits state (if any) and responds with accept/reject within a small bound; if unresponsive, lease can be force-stolen after escalating to eviction coordinator.
   - Implementation primitives (in-memory, low-overhead):
     * Compact lease descriptor: 64-bit struct -> fragment_id(40b), lease_epoch(12b), flags(8b).
     * Atomic CAS: single-word compare-and-swap for lease acquisition and renewals.
     * Lease table sharding: per-core shard of lease table to avoid contention; lookups route to correct shard via fragment_id hash.
   - Interaction with eviction and hot-swap:
     * Eviction requests present in eviction queue; eviction coordinator attempts to acquire lease for fragment before evicting. If lease held, coordinator issues a 'try-transfer' and waits up to transfer-timeout for release.
     * Hot-swap: new model binary registers desired fragments and issues transfer requests for fragments currently leased. Runtime coordinates graceful replacement: unpack new fragment to staging buffer, then request a lease swap; once approved, swap pointer atomically and publish new version. Old holder receives a notification to decrement reference and eventually release.

3) KV-cache and prefetch synergy:
   - When KV-cache hits indicate heavy reuse of particular attention layers' KV fragments, prefetcher raises those fragments' lease durations to avoid eviction while session active.
   - Lease metadata includes a lightweight reference counter for active KV-cache readers; eviction coordinator considers ref-count > 0 as sticky (requires transfer instead of immediate drop).

4) Config and runtime knobs (examples):
   - prefetch.window_ms: 12
   - prefetch.max_fragments_per_request: 6
   - prefetch.bandwidth_pct: 25
   - lease.default_ttl_ms: 2000
   - lease.transfer_timeout_ms: 120
   - lease.max_renewals_per_second: 10
   - staging.deserialize_threshold_confidence: 0.7

5) Telemetry and observability:
   - Metrics to emit:
     * prefetch.attempts_total, prefetch.hits (did prefetch avoid a cold page fault), prefetch.evicted_during_grace
     * lease.acquires_total, lease.renewals_total, lease.transfers_total, lease.forcesteal_total
     * fragment.mmap_page_faults_per_sec, fragment.deserialize_time_ms_p50/p95
     * eviction.wait_ms_distribution (time coordinator waited for lease transfer)
   - Traces: attach fragment_id and model_version to request traces when prefetch or lease transfer occurs.
   - Alerts: high lease.forcesteal_total rate or elevated eviction.wait_ms_p95 indicate mis-tuned TTLs or insufficient memory.

6) Failure modes and mitigations:
   - Unresponsive lease-holder: coordinator escalates by marking fragment as 'contested' and after stale_threshold marks for forcesteal; forcesteal triggers a diagnostic trace and increments metric.
   - Over-aggressive prefetch causing OOM: prefetch budget enforcer evicts lowest-priority prefetched fragments first and reduces prefetch.bandwidth_pct on-the-fly.
   - Race during hot-swap: atomic pointer swap backed by lease guarantees prevents partial reads of mixed-version parameters. Staging buffer holds new fragment until swap success.

7) Testing and rollout plan:
   - Unit tests for lease CAS semantics and soft-expiry behavior.
   - Integration test: synthetic workload with many short sessions touching disjoint fragments to verify prefetch reduces mmap faults and lowers p99 latency.
   - Chaos test: kill lease-holders mid-transfer to validate coordinator forcesteal path and recovery.
   - Canary rollout: enable for single model family in Hosted API region with detailed telemetry for 72 hours, monitor lease.forcesteal_total and prefetch.hits > 30% with no increase in OOM or eviction.wait_ms_p95.

Open questions and future work:
- Can we leverage model topology (attention graph) to improve lookahead accuracy beyond prefix-based heuristics?
- Should leases be location-aware (node-local vs global) to support cross-node cache coherence for Dedicated clusters?
- Investigate ML-based prefetcher as an optional plugin if heuristics plateau.

Appendix: lightweight API sketches
- acquire_lease(fragment_id, desired_ttl_ms) -> {ok, lease_token} | {held_by, expires_at}
- renew_lease(lease_token) -> {ok, new_expiry} | {stale}
- request_transfer(fragment_id, target_worker_id) -> {transfer_pending} (notifies holder)
- force_steal(fragment_id) -> audit-only operation (requires coordinator)

References and related docs:
- internal: weight-residency-metrics (Confluence)
- design notes: predictive-prefetch-telemetry-driven-weight-proxy-spec (serving-runtime folder)
- prior art: OS page cache prefetchers, JVM biased-locking (conceptually similar to leases)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: the goal is to add small, auditable coordination that removes the worst IO tails rather than to centralize control.
- Feedback requested on TTL defaults and transfer_timeouts; early defaults tuned for NVMe-backed hosts.
